parent.name: Los Angeles Athletic Club (LAAC)
parent.description:
For nearly 150 years, the Los Angeles Athletic Club has brought people together through athletics, healthy competition, personal growth, and community. This September, we're putting that spirit to work for an incredible cause.

On September 12, 25 LAAC members will take on the Special Olympics Southern California Plane Pull, working together to pull a 62-ton UPS aircraft 12 feet down the runway. It's a challenge built for us: strength, teamwork, a little friendly competition, and a whole lot of community.

But what we're pulling for matters even more.

Every dollar raised by Team LAAC supports Special Olympics Southern California and helps provide year-round sports training, competition, and opportunities for athletes with intellectual disabilities.

At LAAC, we know athletics can do more than make us stronger. It can create connection, build confidence, bring people together, and help us discover what we're capable of. That's why this partnership feels so right.

We're training together. We're fundraising together. And on September 12, we'll pull together.

Help Team LAAC Pull for a Purpose.

Make a gift to our team, support one of our members, or join us in cheering on Team LAAC and the incredible athletes of Special Olympics Southern California.

Train together. Pull together. Give together.

parent.name: Los Angeles Athletic Club (LAAC)
parent.description:
For nearly 150 years, the Los Angeles Athletic Club has brought people together through athletics, healthy competition, personal growth, and community. This September, we're putting that spirit to work for an incredible cause.

On September 12, 25 LAAC members will take on the Special Olympics Southern California Plane Pull, working together to pull a 62-ton UPS aircraft 12 feet down the runway. It's a challenge built for us: strength, teamwork, a little friendly competition, and a whole lot of community.

But what we're pulling for matters even more.

Every dollar raised by Team LAAC supports Special Olympics Southern California and helps provide year-round sports training, competition, and opportunities for athletes with intellectual disabilities.

At LAAC, we know athletics can do more than make us stronger. It can create connection, build confidence, bring people together, and help us discover what we're capable of. That's why this partnership feels so right.

We're training together. We're fundraising together. And on September 12, we'll pull together.

Help Team LAAC Pull for a Purpose.

Make a gift to our team, support one of our members, or join us in cheering on Team LAAC and the incredible athletes of Special Olympics Southern California.

Train together. Pull together. Give together.

data.name: Billy Lockett
data.description: I love Special Olympics because it has allowed me to play sports year-round. Over the years, I have played Bocce, Bowling, Softball, Golf, Floor Hockey and Cycling. I even had a chance to participate in the World Games in Nebraska once. I am participating in the Special Olympics Southern California Plane Pull on September 12. I did this last year and it was a lot of fun. This is a fun team competition to see which team of 25 can pull a 124,000-pound jet 12 feet the fastest at Long Beach Airport. With your donation, you can help SOSC enrich the lives of athletes with intellectual disabilities and their communities through sports, education, and athlete health. Every dollar raised by Special Olympics supports the provision of equipment, uniforms, and training. Thanks for helping.

parent.name: Los Angeles Athletic Club (LAAC)
parent.description:
For nearly 150 years, the Los Angeles Athletic Club has brought people together through athletics, healthy competition, personal growth, and community. This September, we're putting that spirit to work for an incredible cause.

On September 12, 25 LAAC members will take on the Special Olympics Southern California Plane Pull, working together to pull a 62-ton UPS aircraft 12 feet down the runway. It's a challenge built for us: strength, teamwork, a little friendly competition, and a whole lot of community.

But what we're pulling for matters even more.

Every dollar raised by Team LAAC supports Special Olympics Southern California and helps provide year-round sports training, competition, and opportunities for athletes with intellectual disabilities.

At LAAC, we know athletics can do more than make us stronger. It can create connection, build confidence, bring people together, and help us discover what we're capable of. That's why this partnership feels so right.

We're training together. We're fundraising together. And on September 12, we'll pull together.

Help Team LAAC Pull for a Purpose.

Make a gift to our team, support one of our members, or join us in cheering on Team LAAC and the incredible athletes of Special Olympics Southern California.

Train together. Pull together. Give together.

data.name: Jessica Parker
data.description:
I learned from a young age that sports are about so much more than competition. They bring people together. They build community. They create confidence, belonging, and bonds that can last a lifetime.

That's a big part of why I'm so proud to serve on the Board of Special Olympics Southern California and why I'm especially excited about this year's Plane Pull.

As a member of the Los Angeles Athletic Club, I saw an opportunity to bring two communities I care about together. So this year, we're building Team LAAC: 25 members who will train, fundraise, laugh and ultimately work together to pull a 62-ton airplane down the runway in support of Special Olympics Southern California athletes.

And that's really what I'm most excited about: the together part.

Special Olympics creates opportunities for athletes with intellectual disabilities to compete, grow, build friendships, discover their strength, and experience the joy of belonging to a team. Those opportunities are provided year-round and at no cost to athletes and their families.

On September 12, I'll be pulling alongside my LAAC teammates and our Special Olympics athlete co-captain, Christie. But the 25 of us holding the rope are only one part of our team.

Every person who donates is pulling with us.

Your gift helps Special Olympics Southern California continue creating the kind of experiences I've believed in since I was a kid: places where sports become a doorway to friendship, confidence, community, and belonging.

Thank you for being part of our team.
